A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ROIDA and contain readable main text and Appendices A–H. Text comparison and rendered pages support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables, and appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original D4RL locomotion and manipulation experiments, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and supplementary baseline comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental outcomes in Section 5 and the appendices, including benchmark returns and ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same PU reward learning, thresholded weighted behavioral cloning, and TD learning procedure. Appendix D.1 revises numerical hyperparameters within the existing loss-balancing scheme, without changing its components or algorithmic steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four MuJoCo locomotion environments and four Adroit manipulation tasks using D4RL. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: BC-exp, BC-all, DemoDICE, ORIL, and DWBC remain the comparators in Tables 1, 2, and 6. BCDP remains the additional comparator in Table 9; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 changes β from 0.053 times λ1/λ3 to (0.01/7.5) times λ1/λ3, approximately 40 times smaller. The new α coefficient, also 0.01/7.5, approximates its earlier 0.0013 value. This is a localized revision to reported training settings; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablations, auxiliary-data scalability analysis, reward-threshold sensitivity, ground-truth reward comparison, and η sensitivity study are retained unchanged in Section 5.4 and the appendices.

E5.justification: Both report five random seeds and retain the same tabulated uncertainty reporting and rliable analysis with 95% confidence intervals. Appendix F text moves across page boundaries without changing statistical procedures.

E6.justification: The tables and figures retain identical reported results, including benchmark scores, ablations, supplementary comparisons, and sensitivity findings. The revised loss coefficients are not accompanied by added or revised result entries.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, mathematical assumptions, and Equations 1–6 are unchanged. The appendix edit concerns numerical training hyperparameters rather than a new or revised theoretical argument, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about exploiting diverse auxiliary data and robustness to its quality.

C2.justification: Appendix D.1 newly explains that the 1/7.5 factor emphasizes behavioral cloning on expert data. This adds a limited rationale for loss balancing; interpretations of experimental findings, limitations, and broader impacts remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 revises the implementation recipe for α and β, explicitly specifies the 1/7.5 factor, and explains its purpose. Network architectures, optimizers, hardware, and dataset instructions otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 41 references are unchanged. The added generic attribution of the scaling factor to previous work introduces no specific citation or substantive revision to novelty or research positioning.

P1.justification: Appendix D.1 gains one explanatory sentence and expanded coefficient notation, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The surrounding prose, section order, and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded fractions and explanation in Appendix D.1 cause local reflow across pages 11–14, including a vertical shift of Table 10. Figure designs, table structures, and their contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a useful explanation but substantially changes the reported β coefficient while retaining every result, without explaining whether this corrects documentation or reflects different training runs. The PDFs do not establish which recipe produced the retained outcomes, so the net effect on correctness and reproducibility remains uncertain.
